section: International - summits, conferences and their outcomes
subsections: India's G20 Presidency - theme, venues, edition hosted
Alliances and initiatives launched at summits - founders, India's role
Membership changes - new members admitted, groupings expanded

accepted.s:
With reference to India's G20 Presidency, consider the following statements:
1. India hosted the 18th G20 Summit.
2. The Summit was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
3. The theme of the Summit was “One Earth, One Family, One Future”.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India hosted the 18th G20 Summit at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 9–10 September 2023. Its theme was “One Earth, One Family, One Future”.
accepted.tq: Combine three directly related factual statements and identify the option containing all correct details.
accepted.sec: India's G20 Presidency - theme, venues, edition hosted

accepted.s: The 18th G20 Summit hosted by India was held on:
accepted.x: The 18th G20 Summit was held in New Delhi on 9–10 September 2023.
accepted.tq: Direct date recall using closely spaced date distractors.
accepted.sec: India's G20 Presidency - theme, venues, edition hosted

accepted.s: Which of the following was the headline outcome of the 18th G20 Summit hosted by India?
o: Admission of Timor-Leste as an ASEAN member
Adoption of the Glasgow Climate Pact
Admission of the African Union as a permanent member
Creation of the Loss and Damage Fund
accepted.x: The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G20 during India's Presidency.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the principal summit outcome from outcomes associated with other international groupings or summits.
accepted.sec: India's G20 Presidency - theme, venues, edition hosted

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT launched under India's G20 Presidency?
accepted.x: The Global Biofuels Alliance, MAHARISHI and the Global Initiative on Digital Health were launched under India's G20 Presidency. The Loss and Damage Fund is associated with COP27.
accepted.tq: Find the item belonging to a nearby but different international summit.
accepted.sec: India's G20 Presidency - theme, venues, edition hosted

accepted.s: The MAHARISHI initiative launched under India's G20 Presidency is associated with:
accepted.x: MAHARISHI was launched as an initiative relating to research on millets.
accepted.tq: Match an initiative with its precise subject rather than with another G20 initiative.
accepted.sec: India's G20 Presidency - theme, venues, edition hosted

accepted.s: Which of the following initiatives was launched under India's G20 Presidency specifically for climate monitoring?
accepted.x: A “G20 satellite” was launched under India's G20 Presidency for climate monitoring.
accepted.tq: Direct initiative-purpose discrimination.
accepted.sec: India's G20 Presidency - theme, venues, edition hosted

accepted.s: India's G20 Presidency lasted from:
accepted.x: India held the G20 Presidency from 1 December 2022 to 30 November 2023.
accepted.tq: Test an exact tenure using four closely related date ranges.
accepted.sec: India's G20 Presidency - theme, venues, edition hosted

accepted.s: During India's G20 Presidency, meetings were spread across approximately how many cities covering all States and Union Territories?
accepted.x: G20 meetings during India's Presidency were held across about 60 cities in all States and Union Territories.
accepted.tq: Numerical recall with rounded scale-based distractors.
accepted.sec: India's G20 Presidency - theme, venues, edition hosted

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Initiative)
a. International Solar Alliance
b. CDRI
c. Global Biofuels Alliance
 d. ACITI

List-II (Launch context)
i. India's G20 Presidency, 2023
ii. COP21, Paris, 2015
iii. UN Climate Action Summit, 2019
iv. G20 Johannesburg sidelines, November 2025

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The International Solar Alliance was launched at COP21; CDRI at the 2019 UN Climate Action Summit; the Global Biofuels Alliance during India's 2023 G20 Presidency; and ACITI on the sidelines of G20 Johannesburg in November 2025.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure launch-context pair and eliminate codes.
accepted.sec: Alliances and initiatives launched at summits - founders, India's role

accepted.s: The International Solar Alliance was launched jointly by:
accepted.x: The International Solar Alliance was launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015.
accepted.tq: Direct founder-pair recall with distractors drawn from other initiatives.
accepted.sec: Alliances and initiatives launched at summits - founders, India's role

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the International Solar Alliance is correct?
o: It is headquartered in Stockholm and was founded by India and Sweden.
Its secretariat is at New Delhi and it was launched at COP29 in Baku.
Its headquarters is at Gurugram and it is the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.
It is headquartered in Paris and deals exclusively with nuclear energy.
accepted.x: The International Solar Alliance has its headquarters at Gurugram and is the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.
accepted.tq: Use the headquarters and institutional-status distinction to reject swapped-location options.
accepted.sec: Alliances and initiatives launched at summits - founders, India's role

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. CDRI was launched at the UN Climate Action Summit in 2019.
2. The secretariat of CDRI is located in New Delhi.
3. CDRI is associated with sustainable biofuels.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: CDRI was launched at the 2019 UN Climate Action Summit and has its secretariat in New Delhi. Sustainable biofuels are associated with the Global Biofuels Alliance, not CDRI.
accepted.tq: Identify one swapped subject-area statement among two correct institutional facts.
accepted.sec: Alliances and initiatives launched at summits - founders, India's role

accepted.s: The Digital Innovation Alliance launched at G20 2025 was promoted by:
accepted.x: The Digital Innovation Alliance at G20 2025 was launched by India, Brazil and South Africa as a DPI-based Global South alternative.
accepted.tq: Founder-group identification with country combinations from related initiatives.
accepted.sec: Alliances and initiatives launched at summits - founders, India's role

accepted.s:
The Tropical Forest Forever Facility, associated with COP30, has which of the following features?
1. It is Brazil-led.
2. It involves US$125 billion.
3. India joined it as an Observer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Tropical Forest Forever Facility is Brazil-led, involves US$125 billion, and India joined it as an Observer.
accepted.tq: Check a three-part institutional description without confusing it with the COP outcome itself.
accepted.sec: Alliances and initiatives launched at summits - founders, India's role

accepted.s: LeadIT, co-chaired by India and Sweden at COP29 in Baku, is concerned primarily with:
o: Expansion of solar power in tropical countries
Digital public infrastructure for the Global South
Sharing benefits from digital sequence information
Transition of heavy industry, including steel and cement
accepted.x: LeadIT focuses on the transition of heavy industries such as steel and cement.
accepted.tq: Link the initiative to the sector named in its policy objective.
accepted.sec: Alliances and initiatives launched at summits - founders, India's role

accepted.s: Which of the following proposals was included among India's proposals at G20 2025?
accepted.x: The Africa Skills Multiplier was one of India's G20 2025 proposals, aiming at one million trainers over a decade.
accepted.tq: Separate a national proposal from formal outcomes of climate and biodiversity conferences.
accepted.sec: Alliances and initiatives launched at summits - founders, India's role

accepted.s: The Africa Skills Multiplier proposed by India envisages:
o: One million solar panels in five years
One million digital health workers in one year
One million trainers in a decade
One million hectares of forest by 2030
accepted.x: The Africa Skills Multiplier proposal envisages one million trainers over a decade.
accepted.tq: Test the distinctive numerical target attached to a named proposal.
accepted.sec: Alliances and initiatives launched at summits - founders, India's role

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among India's G20 2025 proposals?
accepted.x: India's proposals included Countering the Drug-Terror Nexus, the Global Traditional Knowledge Repository and the Critical Minerals Circularity Initiative. The Baku-to-Belém Roadmap is associated with COP29.
accepted.tq: Find the outcome belonging to another summit and subject cluster.

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the expansion of BRICS?
1. BRIC was coined in 2001 by Jim O'Neill.
2. South Africa joined in 2011.
3. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE joined in 2024.
4. Indonesia joined in January 2025.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Jim O'Neill coined BRIC in 2001; South Africa joined in 2011; Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE joined in 2024; and Indonesia joined in January 2025.
accepted.tq: Build the chronology of membership changes from the earliest coinage to the latest admission.
accepted.sec: Membership changes - new members admitted, groupings expanded

accepted.s: Which country was invited to BRICS but had not formally confirmed its membership?
accepted.x: Saudi Arabia was invited to BRICS but had not formally confirmed its membership, although some listings count it as a member.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between invitation, formal confirmation and listing practice.
accepted.sec: Membership changes - new members admitted, groupings expanded

accepted.s: Apart from its full-member count, the expanded BRICS grouping includes approximately how many partner countries?
accepted.x: The expanded BRICS grouping is described as having approximately 10 partner countries, including Belarus, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand and Vietnam.
accepted.tq: Recall the numerical distinction between full members and partner countries.
accepted.sec: Membership changes - new members admitted, groupings expanded

accepted.s: Which of the following countries is listed as an example of a BRICS partner country?
accepted.x: Belarus is among the examples of BRICS partner countries; Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand and Vietnam are other examples.
accepted.tq: Identify a member of a named partner grouping rather than a full member or unrelated major economy.
accepted.sec: Membership changes - new members admitted, groupings expanded

accepted.s: The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G20 in 2023 and was fully operationalised at:
accepted.x: The African Union's permanent membership in the G20 was fully operationalised at Johannesburg in 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of admission from the later operationalisation of membership.
accepted.sec: Membership changes - new members admitted, groupings expanded

accepted.s: Timor-Leste became the 11th member of ASEAN and attended its first summit as a full member in:
accepted.x: Timor-Leste became ASEAN's 11th member and attended its first summit as a full member in October 2025.
accepted.tq: Direct membership-and-date recall using adjacent years as distractors.
accepted.sec: Membership changes - new members admitted, groupings expanded

accepted.s: The East Asia Summit currently has:
accepted.x: The East Asia Summit has 19 members, comprising 11 ASEAN members and 8 partners.
accepted.tq: Split the total into its two components before selecting the matching composition.
accepted.sec: Membership changes - new members admitted, groupings expanded

accepted.s: Russia's position in the G7/G8 framework is correctly described by which statement?
o: It was admitted in 1998 and suspended in 2014 after Crimea.
It was admitted in 2014 and suspended in 1998 after Crimea.
It was never admitted to the G8.
It became a permanent G7 member in 2024.
accepted.x: Russia was admitted in 1998, creating the G8, and was suspended in 2014 after the Crimea episode.
accepted.tq: Arrange the two membership events in their correct historical sequence.
accepted.sec: Membership changes - new members admitted, groupings expanded

accepted.s:
Match the following Climate COPs with their venues and principal outcomes:
A. COP21
B. COP26
C. COP27
D. COP28

1. Glasgow Climate Pact and India's Panchamrit
2. Paris Agreement
3. Loss and Damage Fund
4. Global Stocktake and “transition away” from fossil fuels

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: COP21 in Paris produced the Paris Agreement; COP26 in Glasgow produced the Glasgow Climate Pact; COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh produced the Loss and Damage Fund; and COP28 in Dubai produced the Global Stocktake and the “transition away” wording.
accepted.tq: Start with the well-known Paris Agreement pair and complete the summit-outcome matches.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: The Paris Agreement was adopted on 12 December 2015 and entered into force on:
accepted.x: The Paris Agreement was adopted on 12 December 2015 and entered into force on 4 November 2016.
accepted.tq: Distinguish adoption and entry-into-force dates rather than treating them as one event.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: India's Panchamrit was associated with:
accepted.x: India's Panchamrit was associated with COP26, held at Glasgow in 2021.
accepted.tq: Match a national climate initiative with the correct COP venue and year.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: The Loss and Damage Fund was associated with:
accepted.x: The Loss and Damage Fund was an outcome associated with COP27 at Sharm el-Sheikh in 2022.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among successive COP outcomes.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal outcome of COP28?
o: Adoption of the Glasgow Climate Pact
Adoption of the Paris Agreement and entry into force provisions
Global Stocktake and the call for a “transition away” from fossil fuels
Creation of the Loss and Damage Fund
accepted.x: COP28 in Dubai produced the Global Stocktake and included the wording on transitioning away from fossil fuels.
accepted.tq: Use the exact outcome phrase to distinguish COP28 from COP26 and COP27.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding COP29:
1. It was held at Baku.
2. It set a new collective quantified finance goal of US$300 billion annually by 2035.
3. It proposed the Baku-to-Belém Roadmap to US$1.3 trillion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: COP29 was held at Baku in 2024. Its outcomes included the US$300 billion annual finance goal by 2035 and the Baku-to-Belém Roadmap targeting US$1.3 trillion.
accepted.tq: Combine venue, acronym-related finance outcome and numerical target in one coded question.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: COP30 was held at Belém, Brazil, and was notable because it was:
o: The first COP held under the UNFCCC
The first COP held in a G7 country
The first COP held in Europe
The first COP held in the Amazon
accepted.x: COP30, held in Belém in November 2025, was the first COP held in the Amazon region.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive geographical feature of the venue.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the Belém Political Package of COP30?
o: A roadmap for the complete phase-out of fossil fuels
Belém Action Mechanism on just transition
60 indicators for the Global Goal on Adaptation
accepted.x: The COP30 outcomes included tripling adaptation finance by 2035, the Belém Action Mechanism and 60 Global Goal on Adaptation indicators. No fossil-fuel roadmap was adopted.
accepted.tq: Locate the precise exception among several outcomes from the same summit.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: The phrase “global mutirão” is associated with the:
accepted.x: “Global mutirão” formed part of the Belém Political Package adopted at COP30.
accepted.tq: Test recognition of a distinctive official phrase and its summit context.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct pairing regarding future Climate COPs?
accepted.x: COP31 is scheduled for Antalya, Türkiye, in November 2026, while COP32 is scheduled for Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in 2027.
accepted.tq: Match consecutive future editions with their venues without reversing the sequence.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s:
With reference to COP31, consider the following statements:
1. Türkiye holds the presidency.
2. Australia presides over the negotiations.
3. It is scheduled for November 2026 at Antalya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: COP31 is scheduled for November 2026 at Antalya, Türkiye; Türkiye holds the presidency and Australia presides over the negotiations.
accepted.tq: Separate host-country presidency from the country presiding over negotiations.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: Which statement regarding India's proposed hosting of COP33 is correct?
o: India won the bid and will host COP33 in 2028.
India has hosted COP33 and is bidding for COP34.
India withdrew its bid, leaving South Korea as the only other contender.
India withdrew its bid after COP21, leaving Brazil as the only contender.
accepted.x: India withdrew its COP33 bid through an Environment Ministry letter dated 2 April 2026, reported on 9 April 2026; South Korea was the only other contender.
accepted.tq: Use the status of a bid rather than assuming that a bid means successful hosting.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: How many times has India hosted a UN Climate Change COP, according to the given record?
o: Three times, COP8, COP26 and COP33
accepted.x: India has hosted only COP8, held in 2002.
accepted.tq: Distinguish hosting from participation, bidding or association with another COP outcome.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly matches the biodiversity COP outcome?
o: CBD COP16—Cali Fund on digital sequence information benefit-sharing
accepted.x: CBD COP16 at Cali, resumed at Rome, was associated with the Cali Fund on digital sequence information benefit-sharing. COP15 produced the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.
accepted.tq: Separate biodiversity-convention outcomes from UNFCCC climate outcomes.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework is associated with the target popularly known as:
accepted.x: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework is associated with the 30x30 target.
accepted.tq: Recall the numerical shorthand attached to a named international framework.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: The first Convention on Biological Diversity COP was held at:
accepted.x: The first CBD COP was held at Nassau, Bahamas, in 1994.
accepted.tq: Direct venue-and-year recall with later biodiversity COP venues as distractors.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC):
1. It was adopted on 9 May 1992 at the Rio Earth Summit.
2. It entered into force on 21 March 1994.
3. It has 198 Parties.
4. Its secretariat is located at Bonn.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The UNFCCC was adopted on 9 May 1992 at the Rio Earth Summit, entered into force on 21 March 1994, has 198 Parties and has its secretariat at Bonn.
accepted.tq: Test a complete treaty profile through date, membership and headquarters statements.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome

accepted.s: At the Bonn Subsidiary Bodies session in June 2026, India pressed for dialogue on unilateral trade measures such as:
accepted.x: India pressed at the June 2026 Bonn Subsidiary Bodies session for dialogue on unilateral trade measures such as the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).
accepted.tq: Identify the policy instrument from a current climate-negotiation context.
accepted.sec: Climate COPs → venue + agreement outcome
